topic: Specialized Structures of Terrestrial and Aquatic Plants
key_concepts: Specialized structures help plants adapt to their environment.
Terrestrial plants live and grow on land.
Roots anchor terrestrial plants and absorb water and nutrients.
Xerophytes are land plants adapted to very dry conditions.
Thick waxy cuticles and fleshy water-storing stems help xerophytes reduce water loss.
Thorns and hairs are specialized structures of some terrestrial plants.
Aquatic plants or hydrophytes live in water.
Big flat leaves help aquatic plants get enough sunlight.
Enlarged air spaces allow aquatic plants such as water hyacinth to float.
Aquatic plant leaves lack a waxy coat and absorb dissolved nutrients efficiently.
The amount of water affects plant growth, and overwatering can harm plants.
